rubric.note: the normative source for what counts as a violation; LABELING.md adds procedure only

reporting.sample_size_rule: ceil(M / p): M is min_true_violations, p is the prevalence the pilot measures
reporting.below_the_bar: print x/n and no percentage; the level joins no comparison

measured_prevalence.measured_by: tests/corpus/pilot: 60 units stratified on raw_end_column, three model families, two rounds, then adjudicated

round_2_settled.note: one unit left the sample as a sampling defect, and seven referrals were decided by the maintainer

measured_prevalence.note: both kinds are labeled on the same units, so the scarcer kind sets the size; three estimates span 58 to 75 and the largest is taken

sample_size_taken.why_less: the rule's 75 is driven entirely by how rare a fused line is; half of it buys every per-level wrap rate and gives up every per-level fused rate, which is the marginal least likely to be usable
consequences: fused recall is reportable for the corpus entire and for no single level: about 6 true fused lines per level against a floor of 10

wrap recall is reportable per level only while recall stays near the pilot's 82%; a level where recall falls to 70% widens past the 15-point half-width and prints x/n instead, so the levels where the detector does worst are the levels least likely to carry a number
a level that turns out unreportable can be topped up on its own: the draw is deterministic and additive, so nothing needs redrawing or relabeling

recall_floors.note: a calibration floor is the rate measured on this corpus, rounded down to two places, so any loss of recall fails a run instead of passing quietly; a holdout floor is a prediction stated before the holdout was labeled

holdout_basis.1: the lower end of the calibration interval for each kind, 0.689 for both, rounded down; the holdout is three unseen projects, so the prediction is the weaker end of what this corpus supports rather than its point estimate
holdout_basis.2: the lower end of the calibration interval for each kind as it stands after the code-span repair, 0.708 for wrap and 0.689 for fused, rounded down; the calibration rates behind them are 169 of 220 and 31 of 37, and the wrap floor is two points above round 1 because that repair raised the rate it derives from; stated before this round was drawn, so no unit of it existed when the number was chosen
holdout_basis.3: the lower end of the calibration interval for each kind, unchanged from round 2 because neither unscored repair moved a calibration rate: 0.708 for wrap against 169 of 220 and 0.689 for fused against 31 of 37, rounded down; the round exists to score the fence repair and the markup repair, both of which add findings the calibration corpus cannot reach, so the floors carry no credit for either; stated before any unit of this round existed

holdout_misses.note: a floor stated before a holdout round and missed by it is acknowledged here, naming what the miss is attributed to, what it blocks, and whether it can still be diagnosed; a round that misses a floor and says nothing here fails the suite, because a missed prediction that nobody writes down is read by the next reader as a pass; an acknowledgement for a round that has not been scored fails too, since that would excuse a floor before it was answered

2.problem: fused: 50 of 77 is 0.649, below the floor of 0.68
2.attributed_to: the fused heuristic on unseen Markdown, and to nothing this release changed: a fused finding is a regex over one line, the only positive test this release altered is the trailing code span peel, and that peel is read at exactly one call site inside the wrap branch, so no edit in this release can move a fused count by one unit; the loss is entirely in Markdown, 25 of 47 against 66 of 79 in round 1, while Go rose to 25 of 30
2.blocks: any published fused recall rate, and any claim that a later repair to the fused heuristic works; it does not block the code-span repair, which is scored against the wrap floor that repair raised and cleared at 219 of 276
2.diagnosable: not from this round: its labels were sealed and deleted when the bundle was spent, so localizing the loss needs the calibration side or a third round

repair_admission.denominator: a unit is scored when it carries a frozen acceptable set and is not ambiguous; ambiguous units leave the rate and are kept as cases, as the label corpus already treats them
repair_admission.activation: a class admits a repair only where every other class is absent, so it is scored on the exact class sets it activates rather than on every unit carrying it
repair_admission.statistic: per activated exact set, the fraction of that stratum's scored units whose machine repair is in the acceptable set
repair_admission.test: every activated stratum clears the floor on its own lower bound, independently of the others
repair_admission.pooling: a population-weighted combination across the activated strata is reported as description, and it decides nothing; one interval over a weighted mean would need a stratified variance estimator this corpus does not define, and several units can share one window and so one repair outcome, which a binomial interval would count as independent trials
repair_admission.unreportable_stratum: an activated stratum the frozen rules cannot rate refuses the class, and is never dropped so that the remaining strata carry the claim

reportable.min_scored_note: a preregistered policy minimum rather than a derivation; what the frozen rules make reportable depends on the realized count, the half-width and the ambiguous fraction, none of them known before labeling, so nothing can prove a smaller stratum intrinsically unreportable; 26 is the size at which a rate of 0.80 first fits inside the frozen half-width, and it is taken as a floor on that ground alone

repair_admission.same_algorithm: the repair transformation under test is applied to the shipped class as well, and both numbers are reported from that one algorithm; a round that scores two classes through two algorithms is refused

zero_tolerance.prose_not_preserved: a machine repair that does not preserve the prose
zero_tolerance.carrier_changed: a machine repair that changes a carrier
zero_tolerance.fired_where_only_the_original_is_accepta: a machine repair that fires on a unit whose acceptable set holds only the original; automatically repairing a line that should have been left alone is the worst outcome this tool can produce

repair_admission.baseline: the shipped class is measured and reported beside every candidate as context; it is 34 boundaries with 32 of them in one source, and it is never the bar
repair_admission.admissible_from: no class is admissible on the calibration side; every number above is scored on a holdout round drawn after the widened predicate is frozen

raw: Only when the enclosing function is about to return does `try` test for an error returned by `f`. Without changes to the behavior of `try`, such an error might then overwrite another error currently being returned by the enclosing function. This is at best confusing, and at worst error-prone. Therefore we suggest to disallow `try` as the called function in a `defer` statement as well. We can always revisit this decision if sensible applications are found.

There is further discussion of this in the [instantiation](#instantiation) section below.

raw: A new `Instantiate` function is added to allow the creation of type and function instances. The `orig` argument supplies the parameterized `*Named` or `*Signature` type being instantiated, and the `targs` argument supplies the type arguments to be substituted for type parameters. It is an error to call `Instantiate` with anything other than a `*Named` or `*Signature` type for `orig`, or with a `targs` value that has length different from the number of type parameters on the parameterized type; doing so will result in a non-nil error being returned.

raw: Type parameter names are represented by a `*TypeName` with a `*TypeParam`-valued `Type()`. They are declared by type parameter lists, or by type parameters on method receivers. Type parameters are scoped to the type or function declaration on which they are defined. Notably, this introduces a new `*Scope` for parameterized type declarations (for parameterized function declarations the scope is the function scope). The `Obj()` method returns the `*TypeName` corresponding to the type parameter (its receiver). The `Index()` method returns the index of the type parameter in its type parameter list, or `-1` if the type parameter has not yet been bound to a type.

raw: The `command/resolve` request is sent from the client to the server to check whether a command is ready for execution or requires additional user input. Before executing any command that supports interactive resolution, the client must call `command/resolve` at least once to determine if the command arguments are comprehensive. As long as the `ExecuteCommandParams` contains non-empty `formFields` (questions), the client should not execute the command. Instead, the client should collect the user's answers and call `command/resolve` with the answers populated in `formAnswers`.

With the compiler split into packages with clearly defined boundaries, it should be straightforward to introduce a new middle representation between the architecture-independent unordered tree (Node*s) and the architecture-dependent ordered list (Prog*s) used today. That representation, which should be architecture-independent but contain information about precise order of execution, can be used to introduce order-dependent but architecture-independent optimizations like elimination of redundant nil checks and bounds checks. It may be based on SSA and if so would certainly take advantage of the lessons learned from Alan Donovan’s go.tools/ssa package.

raw: _Discard the current compilers and use gccgo (or go/parser + go/types + LLVM, or …)_. The current compilers are a large part of Go’s flexibility. Tying development of Go to a comparatively larger code base like GCC or LLVM seems likely to hurt that flexibility. Also, GCC is a large C (now partly C++) program and LLVM a large C++ program. semantic-linefeeds: 2 issue(s) in testdata/chunkplugin/main.go:
  [fused] line 60: two sentences on one line — one sentence per line
         > The lines a test greps for. Each carries the number that ...
  [wrap] line 60: ends mid-clause (column-wrapped?) — break at sentence or clause boundaries, not at a column
         > The lines a test greps for. Each carries the number that ...
Fix these in the block you just wrote: one sentence per line; split sentences over ~120 chars at a real clause boundary (both sides must stand alone); never break URLs, directives, or example code. A finding can be a false positive (e.g. an 'and' joining a compound object is not a boundary) — judge each one; leave the line alone if the break would sever a clause. A wrap finding sharing a line with a blocking one says where the split leaves text, not that a second repair is due: rejoin before you split, so the opening it names travels to the line below. Judge it like any other finding — if that line already ends at a real clause boundary, split without moving anything. If unsure of the rules, load the semantic-linefeeds skill.

main.cost: every rate is recall over the prose the extractor yields, never recall over prose at large

out_of_scope.enumerated_by: every comment block and every Markdown paragraph, restricted to units the extractor never yields
out_of_scope.cost: reported on its own and never merged into the main rates, because extraction scope and judgment error are different failures

protocol_notes: the session that labels the holdout has seen its contents, so it must not be the session that later tunes a predicate; nothing enforces this
losing the passphrase destroys the holdout
source selection may not be conditioned on detector output
each side carries both a wide and a narrow wrapping column: calibration 78/72/68, holdout round 1 71/78/78, holdout round 2 72/75/78
the nine sources belong to nine distinct organizations, so a holdout failure cannot be explained by a second author alone
each side pairs one Go library with one corpus of language design proposals, because the holdout tests generalization to unseen projects rather than unseen genres
rust-lang/rfcs is offered under Apache-2.0 or MIT; Apache-2.0 is the one taken here
pairwise agreement in the pilot ran 93% to 100% across families, so agreement discriminates little on this material and is not evidence of quality

the ambiguous answer was rare and its rarity has two causes, only one of which was fixed: the procedure had told labelers what an ambiguous answer costs the measurement, and removing that raised ambiguous votes from 3 to 9 out of 360

the remaining cause is structural: in both rounds every ambiguous vote arrived alongside a refutation from another labeler, 9 of 9, so the resolution table sent all of them to adjudication and no unit has ever carried the ambiguous label; the rule withholding a rate from a level above 25% ambiguous has never been able to fire
the first units ever to carry the ambiguous label came from adjudication rather than from the resolution table, one per kind, at 2% of the sample

a licence header reached the sampling frame because the enumerator did not apply the licence cut the checker applies; the enumerator now applies it, and the one unit already drawn is marked a sampling defect instead of being relabeled

the expected status on every true violation was computed by running the checker over each source at the commit pinned above, and never earlier than labeling; sampling and labeling stayed blind to detector output
every unit stores the raw lines of its window, so the checker can be rerun over it without the source checkouts; the offline replay agreed with the in-situ verdict on all 54 frozen statuses
a replayed window of comment lines would read as a file's leading licence region, so the replay puts one non-comment line in front of it

markdown nesting of two has four boundaries in a population of 41,307, because the extractor strips at most one blockquote marker and one list marker; that level can never carry a rate, and the four units are guarded per unit instead

raw_end_column was given a quota although the design expects it to spread on its own: its widest band is 2.7% of the population, and filling it by chance would need a base four times the size of the whole corpus

agy returned short arrays on three calibration batches, dropping one unit each; those three batches were rerun in full and the second answers are the recorded ones, because a rerun is a fresh process that never sees its own earlier reply

the extractor skips a four-space-indented line but not the same line inside a blockquote, so Markdown code blocks written as quoted indented text reach the detector as prose; the corpus found this and two of its units are labeled not-a-violation with the detector complaining about them

the list-item break moved two labeled wrap violations from detected to an accepted miss, go-proposal:README.md:118#wrap and go-proposal:design/go2draft-error-values-overview.md:76#wrap; both are lists whose items complete one sentence, so the repair that removed four false positives at list boundaries costs these two detections, and the floors below were lowered to the new rates rather than the repair being withdrawn

the wrapping columns of the first six sources were measured by a script nobody kept; the instrument is now tests/corpus/qualify.py, and replaying it over the same six commits reproduces five of the six columns within two and disagrees with client_golang by eight, so a column is comparable within a round and not across the two

the three round 1 holdout sources were read by the sessions that repaired what that round found, so they are spent; a holdout source declares the round it belongs to and a spent round is never drawn from again
parti is pinned at a commit dated three weeks before this plugin existed, so no hook of this project can have shaped the comments the round 2 sample is drawn from
swiftlang/swift-evolution is Apache-2.0 with a runtime library exception; the exception grants additional permission for compiled binaries and does not reach this prose

a //go:build directive above a block-comment licence header defeats the licence cut: the same header with the directives removed yields no boundaries at all, and with them yields six; 39 of the 387 boundaries drawn for round 2 are Apache boilerplate reached this way, and they were kept as units rather than marked sampling defects because the enumerator and the checker share without_license_text, so the checker is not structurally unable to report them
the generated-file test reads the first five lines of a file, so a DO NOT EDIT marker placed under a licence header is missed; four round 2 boundaries come from protoc-generated Go this way

all three round 2 false positives were recorded as one class, source code reaching the prose stream from Markdown written with HTML entities, and repairing them showed that only two are: both sit inside a <pre> block in one proposal, and the third sits inside a fenced block that the extractor believed was closed

a code fence was closed by a run of the other mark, or by a shorter run of its own, so one tilde line inside a backtick block inverted every fence after it in that file; the correction is the only one of the four repairs that adds findings as well as removing them, because prose the inversion was skipping is checked again, and it has not been scored on prose nobody tuned against

one labeling family answered 14 of the 15 units in a batch and dropped the same unit on four independent runs, including one with an enforced reply shape; that boundary carries a labeling defect and left the sample, because a unit judged by two of three blind passes reads as unanimity wherever those two agree
pairwise agreement between families on round 2 ran 82% to 92%, against 93% to 100% in the pilot, so this material discriminates between labelers where the pilot material did not

round 2 sent 117 of 772 records to adjudication against 27 of 718 on the calibration side; 67 of the 117 were the licence class and 26 were source code that reached the prose stream, so the referral rate measures two extraction defects more than it measures labeler disagreement

the markup repair was tuned in the session that orchestrates round 3, against the calibration side and the two spent draws rebuilt from their pinned public sources; the round 3 draw, labeling passes, and seal therefore run in sessions that did not tune it, the orchestrating session never reads the drawn prose, and the adjudicator is the maintainer

tests/corpus/qualify.py does not exclude YAML front matter, so a Markdown repository carrying front matter on nearly every file collapses to a near-zero mode with most lines far past it; kubernetes/enhancements, kubernetes/website, and nodejs/nodejs.org were set aside for round 3 on that collapse rather than on any measured wrapping habit, and a front-matter cut belongs to the instrument before such a source is ever qualified

GitHub's licence detector reports NOASSERTION for carbon-lang; its LICENSE file opens by declaring the Apache License v2.0 with LLVM Exception, which is why the manifest records it as permitting this use

at the 47 true Markdown fused units round 2 drew, the Wilson interval half-width is 0.137, wide enough to hide a modest repair; round 3 keeps the draw procedure identical to the calibration draw anyway, because a round drawn by a different procedure measures the procedure as well as the predicate, and a Markdown fused stratum too wide to publish is withheld by the existing reporting rule rather than resized for

round 3 cleared both floors it stated, 213 of 260 wrap and 69 of 82 fused against 0.70 and 0.68, and its Markdown fused stratum returned 50 of 59 where round 2 returned 25 of 47; the two intervals are disjoint, which does not adjudicate whether round 2's gap was its draw or the proxy, since round 3 runs the repaired predicate over a different source, but it does establish a publishable fused rate for the predicate that ships

round 3 sent 14 of 712 records to adjudication against round 2's 117 of 772, and the fall measures the extraction repairs more than the material: the licence and code classes that carried round 2's referrals are gone, and what remains is five licence-boilerplate units from carbon-lang's HTML comment header, one gofail directive boundary, five genuine mid-line sentence breaks, and two comma-at-clause-boundary wrap disputes

carbon-lang opens every Markdown file with a licence block inside an HTML comment, and those lines reach the prose stream; the five drawn units were kept and labeled false on the round-2 boilerplate precedent, and the block's presence in the stream is an extraction defect recorded here for a repair no earlier than round 3 being spent

a gofail: directive line and the code line under it reach the prose stream from a Go comment, etcd:server/storage/backend/backend.go:617; the unit was kept and labeled false, the detector reports a wrap there, and that false positive is owned by the directive class rather than by any repair this round scored

round 3's four false positives in 360 labeled non-violations are one directive line and three of one class: adjacent telegraphic notes in Go comments, each note a complete thought without terminal punctuation, where the next note's lowercase opening reads as a severed continuation; that is the non-connector continuation weakness ADR-0002 records, measured here at etcd:server/etcdserver/api/v3rpc/maintenance.go:169, etcd:server/storage/mvcc/metrics.go:242, and etcd:server/storage/wal/metrics.go:26

one labeling family refused one unit in each of two round 3 batches on three consecutive runs, then answered both on a fourth run whose prompt named refusal as unavailable and pointed at the ambiguous answer; recorded beside round 2's same phenomenon, which ended with the refused unit leaving the sample as a defect

the round that scores a widened automatic repair is round 4, and it is stated here before it is drawn. It draws three sources, none of the twelve this manifest already declares (three calibration and nine holdout across rounds 1 to 3), with the same composition split and qualified by qualify.py on line-length distribution alone. It is drawn only after the widened predicate and the admission contract are frozen against it, which binds the admission contract, the class taxonomy, the draw configuration and the source selection together (ADR-0024). And it is drawn, labeled and sealed by a session that did not tune that predicate. No class is admissible before that round answers, because every number the repair corpus holds is measured on the calibration side

units.upper: **Command Layer (Recommended, Prototype Implementation)**: We recommend the **Command layer** (`command/resolve` or generalized `<method>/resolve`) as the primary path. Beyond text edits, it supports non-edit capabilities such as interactive test runners (profiling/coverage options), analysis tools (`govulncheck`), webviews, and CLI tools. Because resolution fires only upon explicit user action, it avoids eager hover issues in clients like Visual Studio. It also avoids making server-to-client `workspace/applyEdit` requests blocking, eliminating RPC timeouts and snapshot memory retention. Its main limitation is that interactive code action must use a command payload rather than resolving purely to edits.
units.lower: **WorkspaceEdit Layer (Alternative)**: We keep the **WorkspaceEdit layer** (`workspaceEdit/resolve`) detailed as an alternative.
